quizzes.stem: A description reads only "Release helper", and Claude never loads that skill when users ask for a changelog. What is the first fix?

options.a: Raise the tool grant so that the skill may run any shell command
options.b: State what it does and when to use it, in everyday words
options.c: Move the folder into the enterprise location so it takes priority
options.d: Add the value true on the model-invocation field in the frontmatter

explanation.b: The page says the description is "What the skill does and when to use it. Claude uses this to decide when to apply the skill."
explanation.c: Ruled out because location decides which skill wins when "two skills share a name", and has no bearing on whether Claude matches a request.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the table says `true` "stops Claude from starting it by itself", which is the opposite of what the team wants.
explanation.a: Ruled out because a tool grant is for "Tools Claude may use without asking while the skill runs", and a skill that is never loaded never runs.

quizzes.stem: A team needs to guarantee that no agent pushes to the main branch, whatever Claude decides in a given turn. Which extension fits best?

options.a: A memory line, which loads as persistent context in each conversation
options.b: A skill, which holds instructions that Claude may follow
options.c: A hook, which runs as a program on every matching event
options.d: A subagent, which is an isolated context returning summaries

explanation.c: The page says "A rule that must never be broken belongs in a hook or a deny rule", and a hook is "a program that always runs".
explanation.a: Ruled out because the table calls it "Persistent context loaded every conversation" for conventions, which is guidance Claude may still get wrong, and the page says a rule that must never be broken needs a hook or a deny rule.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "a skill is instructions Claude may follow", and an instruction that may be followed is not a guarantee.
explanation.d: Ruled out because a subagent is "An isolated context that returns summarised results" for "A side task that would flood the conversation", and not a gate that every command must pass.

quizzes.stem: A skill tags a release and creates a GitHub release. Which frontmatter is right?

options.a: Automatic invocation off, with two command patterns pre-approved
options.b: Automatic invocation on, with the whole Bash tool pre-approved
options.c: Automatic invocation on, with the two command patterns pre-approved
options.d: Automatic invocation off, with the whole Bash tool pre-approved

explanation.a: The page says a task skill with side effects should set `disable-model-invocation: true`, and that `allowed-tools: Bash(git tag *) Bash(gh release create *)` "approves two command families".
explanation.b: Ruled out because the page says bare `Bash` "approves every shell command for that turn".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "a person should start it" when a skill has side effects.
explanation.d: Ruled out because it keeps the person in control but the page says bare `Bash` "turns a narrow skill into an open one".

quizzes.stem: A reviewer subagent's file has no `tools` line. What can it do?

options.a: Read only, because a review of code needs nothing more than reading it
options.b: Nothing at all, because an empty list gives the subagent no tools to use
options.c: Use every tool of the session, including editing and running commands
options.d: Use only the tools that the main conversation allows without asking first

explanation.c: The page says "Omit it and the subagent inherits every tool", and "a reviewer with no `tools` line can edit files and run commands".
explanation.a: Ruled out because a reviewer is bounded only when you list `Read`, `Grep` and `Glob`, as the page says: "Bound a subagent by listing its tools."
explanation.b: Ruled out because the table says "Omit it and the subagent inherits every tool", which is the opposite of none.
explanation.d: Ruled out because a subagent has "specific tool access, and independent permissions", and an omitted list does not narrow it to the main conversation's pre-approvals.

quizzes.stem: A hook script is meant to stop `git push`. Which behaviour stops the call?

options.a: Exiting with code 2 with the reason written to standard error
options.b: Printing a warning to standard output and exiting with code 1
options.c: Exiting with code 0 after logging the command to a file
options.d: Exiting with code 3 after writing a reason to standard error

explanation.a: The page says "Exit 2: Claude Code blocks the action. Write a reason to stderr."
explanation.b: Ruled out because with an exit code of 1 and plain-text output "the action proceeds as a non-blocking error", and a warning does not stop the call.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "Exit 0: no objection", and a logging hook "does not weaken a guard hook" and does not block either.
explanation.d: Ruled out because exit code 3 is an "other exit code", and the page says to "Treat it as a bug in the hook, because it does not stop the call."

quizzes.stem: A subagent builds notes on a repository, and teammates should receive them through version control. Which `memory` value fits?

options.a: `user`, whose directory sits in each person's home folder
options.b: `local`, whose directory is kept out of commits
options.c: `team`, whose directory is shared by every teammate
options.d: `project`, whose directory is committed alongside the sources

explanation.d: The table says the `project` scope, at `.claude/agent-memory/<name>/`, is for knowledge that is "shareable via version control".
explanation.a: Ruled out because the `user` scope is for a case where "The agent should remember across all projects", and its directory is under `~/.claude/`, outside the repository.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the `local` scope is for knowledge that is "project-specific and should not be checked in".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the field takes one of three values, and the page's own example is flagged: "memory must be user, project or local".

quizzes.stem: A plugin declares a dependency on `~2.1.0`, and the dependency's maintainer publishes 2.1.4 and then 2.2.0. Which version do the plugin's users receive?

options.a: 2.2.0, because a range always follows the newest release that exists
options.b: 2.1.0, because a range freezes the first version that it matched once
options.c: Neither, because ranges are resolved only for plugins that carry no version
options.d: 2.1.4, because the range takes patch updates and not the 2.2 line

explanation.d: The page says with `~2.1.0` "users who have your plugin installed keep receiving `2.1.x` patches of the dependency and never move to `2.2`."
explanation.a: Ruled out because a pinned range does not follow the newest release: "Without a version constraint, a dependency moves to each new release its marketplace publishes".
explanation.b: Ruled out because the dependency "installs at the highest git tag that satisfies this range", which is 2.1.4 and not the first match.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "resolution is by git tag" for a git-backed dependency, and the object form with a `version` range is how a dependency is constrained.

quizzes.stem: A team wants contributors to get a plugin when they open the repository, with no manual install step. Where does the configuration go?

options.b: The project's `.claude/settings.json`, under two named keys
options.c: The `marketplace.json` catalog, in the entry for that bundle
options.d: Each person's launch command, using the `--plugin-dir` flag

explanation.b: The page says to "set two keys in the repository's `.claude/settings.json`", so that the marketplace and the enabled plugin reach every contributor.
explanation.a: Ruled out because the manifest is "called the manifest, that names the plugin", so it describes the plugin and does not reach contributors who have not installed it.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the catalog is only where plugins are listed, and the page has the repository name it: "Add the marketplace under `extraKnownMarketplaces`, keyed by the marketplace's own `name`".
explanation.d: Ruled out because `--plugin-dir` "loads a plugin for one session without installing it", so it is neither shared nor lasting.

quizzes.stem: An agent file shipped inside a plugin sets `permissionMode: bypassPermissions` to run quietly. What happens?

options.a: The value is dropped at load time, because the loader skips such fields
options.b: The plugin fails to load, because the loader rejects the whole file
options.c: The agent skips every prompt, exactly as the value says it should
options.d: The agent runs quietly, but only in a folder that the person has trusted

explanation.a: The page says "These fields are ignored when loading agents from a plugin."
explanation.c: Ruled out because the fields are "ignored when loading agents from a plugin", so the agent keeps its normal prompts.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "These fields are ignored when loading agents from a plugin", so the file still loads.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the fields are "ignored" whatever the folder, and trust only decides whether `extraKnownMarketplaces` applies. The page names the fix: "Ship the guard in `hooks/hooks.json`."

quizzes.stem: A team pushes fresh commits to a plugin whose manifest still says `"version": "1.0.0"`. What reaches installed users?

options.a: The fresh commits at the next launch, since a push always counts
options.b: The fresh commits once the marketplace entry repeats that number
options.c: The fresh commits, since the commit hash is the version
options.d: The copy they already hold, until the number is raised

explanation.d: The page says users stay on their cached copy until the string changes.
explanation.a: Ruled out because if the version is not changed, "users don't receive them".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Don't set `version` in both `plugin.json` and the marketplace entry", and Claude Code "then uses the manifest value without warning".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the commit hash counts only when neither place sets a version: "When neither is set", the commit SHA of the source.

quizzes.stem: A catalog entry calls a bundle `reviewer-kit`, while the bundle's own manifest says `review-kit`. What happens when someone installs it under the manifest's name?

options.a: An ambiguity message asks which of the two names was meant
options.b: A success message, with the entry name as the skill prefix
options.c: A not-found message naming what was typed
options.d: A success message, once the catalog has been added again

explanation.c: The page says "When the two names differ and someone installs by the manifest name, Claude Code reports `Plugin "<manifest-name>" not found in marketplace "<marketplace>"`."
explanation.a: Ruled out because the entry name is "the key Claude Code writes under `enabledPlugins`", and nothing offers a choice between the two names.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "the manifest name is the prefix of its skills", and the entry name never replaces it.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "When the two names differ and someone installs by the manifest name, Claude Code reports" a failure, and re-adding the catalog changes neither name.

quizzes.stem: A repository's settings turn on a bundle whose catalog entry points at a repository of its own. A contributor trusts the folder and starts a session. What do they see?

options.a: A notice that it is enabled but not installed, until they install it
options.b: The bundle loaded, since trust is the only condition that applies
options.c: A prompt that lists the hooks of the bundle before it installs
options.d: The bundle loaded once the marketplace is added to managed settings

explanation.a: The page says "Each contributor sees `Plugin "<name>" is enabled in project settings but isn't installed here` in the `/plugin` Errors tab until they run `claude plugin install <name>@<marketplace> --scope project`."
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Only a relative-path plugin installs from the file alone".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "Nothing installs, and nothing prompts, until each contributor runs the install."
explanation.d: Ruled out because "A repository's own settings reach only the contributors who trust the folder", which is a different channel from managed settings.

quizzes.stem: A team needs one rule enforced for every command, with an explanation given to Claude, and the rule must hold in every project that installs their tooling. Which design fits?

options.a: A skill in each repository that tells Claude to avoid the action
options.b: A hook in a plugin that blocks with exit code 2 and a reason
options.c: A subagent in the plugin that reviews each command before it runs
options.d: A line in each memory file that forbids the action by its name

explanation.b: The hooks section gives "deterministic control: certain actions always happen rather than relying on the LLM to choose to run them", exit 2 blocks and "Write a reason to stderr", and a plugin carries the hook to every project that enables it.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "a skill is instructions Claude may follow", and not a rule that holds.
explanation.c: Ruled out because a subagent is "An isolated context that returns summarised results" and is not a gate for every command.
explanation.d: Ruled out because a memory file holds "Persistent context loaded every conversation", which is guidance and not enforcement.

quizzes.stem: One skill drafts release summaries, and another tags and ships a release. Which pair of settings fits?

options.a: Automatic loading off for the first, left on for the second
options.b: Automatic loading left on for both, with `Bash` pre-approved on the second
options.c: Automatic loading off for both, with nothing pre-approved on either
options.d: Automatic loading left on for the first, off for the second

explanation.d: The page says "A skill that writes release notes is harmless and Claude can start it when asked", while a skill with side effects needs `disable-model-invocation: true`.
explanation.a: Ruled out because a skill that tags a release "has side effects, and a person should start it", and this reversal leaves that skill to Claude.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "`allowed-tools: Bash` approves every shell command for that turn", and a skill with side effects should not load by itself either.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "Claude loads it by itself when your request matches its description", and the harmless skill gains from that.

quizzes.stem: A repository's `.claude/settings.json` registers a marketplace and enables a plugin, but a new contributor has not yet approved the folder. What happens?

options.a: The entries apply only to managed settings, never to a repository
options.b: The plugin installs at once, because the file is in the repository
options.c: Claude Code ignores the entries without a message until trust is given
options.d: A prompt appears for each plugin, listing its hooks and its scripts

explanation.c: The page says the entries "apply only in a folder the contributor has trusted, and in an untrusted folder Claude Code ignores them without a message."
explanation.b: Ruled out because trust comes first: "A repository cannot install code on a machine that has not trusted it."
explanation.d: Ruled out because the page says "Claude Code ignores them without a message", which describes no prompt.
explanation.a: Ruled out because the page says "the same two keys go in managed settings" for a whole organisation, and the repository's file covers its own contributors.

quizzes.stem: A subagent should review code and remember wording the team prefers, with that knowledge committed with the code. Which fields fit?

options.a: Read-only tools and the project memory scope
options.b: Every tool and the user memory scope
options.c: Read-only tools and the local memory scope
options.d: Every tool and no memory field at all

explanation.a: The page says a reviewer needs `Read`, `Grep` and `Glob`, and that the `project` scope is for knowledge that is "shareable via version control".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Omit it and the subagent inherits every tool", and the `user` scope lives in the home directory and is not committed.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the `local` scope is for knowledge that "should not be checked in".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "Omit it and the subagent inherits every tool", and without `memory` the subagent keeps no knowledge across conversations.

quizzes.stem: A developer selects a built-in style in a settings file with `"outputStyle": "explanatory"`. Replies keep Claude Code's standard wording and no error appears. What is the cause?

options.a: The value must match a name exactly, or the default applies without a message
options.b: The session must be restarted first, because styles are read only at launch
options.c: Project files cannot set a style at all, so the value belongs in the user folder
options.d: A hook must apply the choice on each reply, because settings only suggest it to Claude

explanation.a: The page says "A value that doesn't match a style name exactly, such as `explanatory`, gives you the Default style", with no error.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Claude uses the new style starting with your next message", and a built-in style needs no restart; only a style file created in a running session does.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "A project's own settings files take precedence over that value", so a project file can set a style.
explanation.d: Ruled out because a style is applied by Claude Code itself: "Claude Code sends the active style's instructions with every request", and no hook is involved.

quizzes.stem: A keybindings file sets `ctrl+s` to `null` and `ctrl+c` to a custom action. What results?

options.a: Both keys change as written, and a warning appears on the screen at once
options.b: Ctrl+C is rebound as written, and Ctrl+S keeps stashing the prompt as before
options.c: Ctrl+S is freed, and Ctrl+C keeps its default because it is reserved
options.d: Both keys are freed together, and Ctrl+C then does nothing at all in the chat

explanation.c: The page says `null` "frees the one key it is written against", and that reserved keys cannot be rebound: "These shortcuts cannot be rebound."
explanation.a: Ruled out because Claude Code "writes a warning to the debug log", not to the screen, and the reserved key does not change.
explanation.b: Ruled out because `null` "frees the one key it is written against", so Ctrl+S stops stashing.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "These shortcuts cannot be rebound", and Ctrl+C is reserved, so it keeps interrupting.

quizzes.stem: One developer's `~/.claude/settings.json` names an output style, while the repository's `.claude/settings.json` names a different one. Which does the session use?

options.a: The personal choice, because a developer's own file always wins for that person
options.b: The project's choice, because that level outranks the user level
options.c: Whichever file was saved last, because Claude Code compares modification times
options.d: Neither choice, because a key set at two levels is rejected as a conflict

explanation.b: The page says "Claude Code uses the value from the highest level that sets it", and the shared project settings sit above the user settings.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "A key at a higher level overrides the same key anywhere below it", and the user level is the lowest of the files.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the documentation gives "their order, highest precedence first", and no file date is involved.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "Claude Code uses the value from the highest level that sets it", so two levels are resolved by order and not rejected.
